#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p bin
cat > bin/countlines <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob dotglob
total=0
for f in "$1"/*.log; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    n=$(wc -l < "$f")
    total=$((total + n))
  fi
done
printf '%d\n' "$total"
EOF
chmod +x bin/countlines

preserving.description: Strips any whitespace from the wc output via tr and relies on cat of the glob guarded by a file test, using a trailing-slash-safe directory variable.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p bin
cat > bin/countlines <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob dotglob
dir="${1%/}"
count=0
for f in "$dir"/*.log; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  c=$(cat -- "$f" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
  count=$((count + c))
done
echo "$count"
EOF
chmod +x bin/countlines

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p bin
cat > bin/countlines <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
shopt -s nullglob dotglob
all=("$1"/*.log)
sum=0
for f in "${all[@]}"; do
  if [[ -f $f ]]; then
    sum=$(( sum + $(wc -l < "$f") ))
  fi
done
echo "$sum"
exit 0
EOF
chmod 755 bin/countlines

import datetime
import json

with open("users.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    reader = csv.reader(fh)
    header = next(reader)
    pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(header)}

preserving.description: Builds all records first, then writes them with a single writelines call and extra spaces after separators.

files.solve.py:
import csv
import json

with open("users.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))

out = []
for row in rows:
    month, day, year = row["signup_date"].strip().split("/")
    record = {
        "id": int(row["id"]),
        "name": row["first_name"] + " " + row["last_name"],
        "email": row["email"].lower(),
        "signup": year + "-" + month.zfill(2) + "-" + day.zfill(2),
    }
    out.append(json.dumps(record, separators=(", ", ": ")) + "\n")

with open("users.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.writelines(out)
